newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle weaker, May options expire.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle weaker, May options expire.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled sharply weaker with the spot-May contract falling below support and hitting a new, life-of-contract low.

Traders cited mixed, technically-driven selling throughout the day, which accelerated once May fell below support at its previous support at 75.50 cents. The contract ended down 2.50 cents at 74.55 cents, having ranged from 77.00 to a new contract low of 73.50 cents.
Second-position July ended down 2.30 at 77.45, after hitting a contract low of 77.20 cents. Nearly every deferred month also fell to a new contract low.
Volume was estimated at 4,500 lots compared to Thursday's official 4,040 lots.
Traders said May options expired quietly.
Weak demand and abundant supplies remain the most significant factors in the longer term, analysts said.

Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes noted in her weekly citrus comment that demand has not picked up on the retail level. While movement exceeded 5 million gallons this week, it is not enough to offset strong imports.

Output in the U.S. and Brazil, meanwhile, are projected to climb. The U.S. Department of Agriculture this week revised its estimate for Brazil's current crop estimate to 1.14 million tonnes from 1.06 million tonnes. Output projections for next season were also raised.
"This could lead to a further build in Brazilian inventories at the same time that Florida inventories are also accumulating," Ganes said.
